AttachmentInput.description:
An attachment as submitted.

The byte source is flattened onto the attachment, so unknown-field rejection is enforced by the `AttachmentSource` variants rather than by `deny_unknown_fields` here, which Serde does not allow alongside `flatten`.

oneOf.description: Text supplied directly in the request.
Bytes supplied directly in the request, base64-encoded.
A file on the same machine, read once at import time. Only sources on this machine can use this form, and the path is read exactly once into the case-owned media store rather than referenced later.

digest_sha256.description: The lowercase hex SHA-256 the source claims, verified at import.

media_type.description: The IANA media type the source claims, verified at import.

name.description: A display name, typically the original file name.

size_bytes.description: The size the source claims, verified at import.

AttachmentKind.description: The broad category of an attachment, which decides which backend capabilities a case requires.

oneOf.description: Plain text carried alongside the transcript.
A recording; requires native video input from the backend.
Any other file the destination may need to know about.

Destination.description: Where a completed refinement should be sent.

oneOf.description: Submit the refined prompt to a local Overlord instance.

base_url.description: The loopback base URL of the Overlord instance.

bearer_token.description: The bearer token for the Overlord endpoint.

mission_id.description: The mission the refined prompt belongs to, when known at submission.

objective_id.description: The objective the refined prompt belongs to, when known.

oneOf.description: Write the refined prompt to a local file.

path.description: Absolute path of the file to write.

MessageRole.description: Who produced a transcript message in the source conversation.

oneOf.description: An assistant or agent in the source conversation.
System or instruction text from the source system.
Tool or command output quoted into the conversation.

SecretString.description: A credential. Accepted on submission and never returned, logged, or displayed.

SourceCallback.description:
Where Refinery sends questions for a case that came from a source with its own interface.

The local interface needs no callback: it reads the case's event stream. A source such as Overlord declares one at submission so a question reaches the person where they already are.

bearer_token.description: The bearer token to present, when the source requires one.

questions_url.description: The loopback URL that receives question notifications.

SourceRef.description: Who submitted a case and how to reach them.

callback.description: Where to deliver questions, when the source handles them itself.

instance.description: Which instance of that system, so two Overlord installations on one machine stay distinguishable.

SourceSystem.description: The system that submitted a case.

oneOf.description: An Overlord instance on this machine.
Any other local caller, named by the caller.

messages.description: Messages in the order they occurred, oldest first.

TranscriptMessage.description: One message in a submitted transcript.

author.description: A display name for the author, when the source supplies one.

created_at.description: When the message was produced, in UTC.

id.description: The source system's identifier for this message, when it has one. Carried so a destination can correlate back, never interpreted.

attachments.description: Attachments to import into the case-owned media store.

destination.description: Where the completed result should be sent.

idempotency_key.description: The retry-safe submission key. The same key with equivalent content returns the existing case; the same key with different content is a conflict.

metadata.description: Bounded source-specific correlation data, carried through to delivery and never interpreted.

repository.description: The registered repository the agent may read, when the case is grounded in code. Repositories are registered out of band; a request names one, it never introduces one.

request_id.description: The source's stable identifier for the thing being refined.

schema_version.description: The contract version this request is written against.

source.description: Who submitted, and where questions go.

task_hint.description: A short description of the intended task, when the source has one.
